subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: After a deferred context-engine maintenance task times out and its lane is released, should subsequent same-session maintenance be suppressed until the original worker settles, explicitly supersede the original run, or be allowed to overlap under a defined plugin contract?
rationale: The patch makes lane release and selected core-side fencing safe enough for liveness, but it cannot infer the intended behavior of a still-running public plugin maintenance call or its relationship to a newly scheduled same-session run.

options.title: Keep the timed-out run coalesced
options.body: Retain the session's deferred-maintenance ownership until the original worker settles, preventing a later same-session maintenance run from overlapping it.

options.title: Define explicit supersession
options.body: Allow a replacement run only with a generation or ownership contract that makes the older worker observably obsolete across core and plugin-facing side effects.

options.title: Allow overlap intentionally
options.body: Document and test concurrent same-session maintenance as a supported context-engine plugin contract, including the required side-effect isolation.

recommendation.title: Keep the timed-out run coalesced
recommendation.body: Retain the session's deferred-maintenance ownership until the original worker settles, preventing a later same-session maintenance run from overlapping it.
